messages:
eli: Quick check — planning to enable KV_CACHE_TIER2 for a canary today around 11:30 PT. Target audience: internal orgs + 5% external traffic. Fallback will be the nullcache kernel. Any objections?

maya: +1 from infra. Please make sure we have mem pressure and eviction alerts wired. Also add an automatic rollback condition.

aj: Can you paste the exact rollout config you'll use? cc @frank for the PR review.

eli: Config draft:```yaml
flag: KV_CACHE_TIER2
rollout:
  - audience: internal
    pct: 100
  - audience: external
    pct: 5
fallbacks:
  - kernel: nullcache_kernel
conditions:
  - rollback_if: p95_latency > baseline * 1.15
  - rollback_if: error_rate > 0.005
model_filters:
  blacklist: [redwood-13b-raw, llama-70b]
kernel_allowlist: [kv-cache-friendly, classic]
metrics: [p50_tokens, p95_latency, gpu_mem_pct, oom_count]
canary_window: 2h
```

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary at 2026-03-18T18:30:00Z by eli — status: queued.

frank: I can review the PR in ~30m. Two quick asks: 1) add a hard model_size cap so we don't enable on >40B, 2) make sure the tests include seq_len=1024 perf runs.

sophie: fwiw we saw a regression last week for q4_0 quantized kernels with a similar kv tweak. Recommend restricting to non-quantized kernels for the first canary.

eli: Good catch — I'll add kernel allowlist to avoid quantized kernels and add model_size cap (<=40B). Also making the canary window 2h and realtime rollback if p95 > baseline*1.15 or error_rate > 0.5%.

laura: ops — please confirm alerting: evictions, paging, oom_count, and a canary-specific p95 alert. Ops-bot, can you confirm coverage?

ops-bot: Alert group 'kv-cache-eviction' exists and pages on-call. Added temporary alert 'kv-cache-canary-p95' with threshold = baseline * 1.15 for 5m. Added runbook link: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-cache-canary.

maya: Thanks — any PR/merge ETA? Ping me when merged so I can schedule the deploy window in the calendar.

frank: PR #2345 opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/merge_requests/2345 — includes config, unit tests, and a perf job. Note: perf job currently runs on internal infra, may be slower than prod.

eli: Will run final perf on staging infra and merge if green. Merging in ~10m after tests. Will post a short postmortem if anything surprising. Thanks folks :rocket:
